samples.text:
The table shows how people in five countries spent their money on six different categories in 2022, as a percentage of total spending.

Firstly, leisure was the biggest category in many countries. In Country A it was 36%, which is the highest in the table, and Country B and Country E spent 29% and 28% on it. Country D spent only 20%.

Housing was also important. Country C spent the most on housing with 31%, and Country A and Country E spent 26% and 24%. Country D spend 22% and Country B spent 18%, it was the lowest.

For food and drink, there was big differences. Country D spent 35% of their money on food, which was more than any other category in that country. Country B was 28% but Country A only spent 12%.

Health and education was the smallest categories in all countries. Health was between 3% and 12%, and education was between 2% and 11%.

Overall, leisure and housing took the biggest part of spending, while health and education was small.
samples.why: Main categories covered with accurate figures · overview present but basic and at the end · mechanical, list-like organisation · limited vocabulary range · several agreement and tense errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates how consumer spending was divided among six categories in five countries in 2022, expressed as a percentage of the total.

Overall, leisure and housing accounted for the largest shares of spending in most of the countries, whereas health and education made up the smallest proportions everywhere. Country D was the main exception, as food and drink was its biggest category.

Leisure was the top category in three countries. It represented more than a third of all spending in Country A, at 36%, and slightly less in Country B and Country E, at 29% and 28% respectively. Housing, meanwhile, was the largest item in Country C, at 31%, and took between 18% and 26% of the budget in the other countries.

Spending on food and drink varied widely. Consumers in Country D devoted 35% of their spending to this category, almost three times as much as those in Country A, where the figure was only 12%. In contrast, health and education received relatively little in all five countries. Health spending ranged from 3% in Country D to 12% in Country E, while the proportion spent on education was lowest in Country C at 2% and highest in Country D at 11%.
samples.why: Clear overview with the main exception noted · key features selected and compared · logical progression by category · good range of vocabulary (devoted, accounted for) · mostly error-free, slight repetition of spending.

samples.text:
The table breaks down consumer expenditure in five countries in 2022 into six categories, showing each as a proportion of total spending.

It is clear that spending priorities differed considerably between the countries. Leisure and housing generally absorbed the largest shares, while health and education consistently attracted the least, although Country D departed from the general pattern by spending most heavily on food and drink.

Leisure was the single largest category in Countries A, B and E, accounting for 36%, 29% and 28% of expenditure respectively. In Country A, this was three times the share allocated to food and drink, which, at 12%, was the lowest food figure in the table. Country C, by contrast, spent most on housing (31%), with leisure making up a quarter of its total.

Country D presents a notably different profile. Food and drink made up 35% of its spending, well ahead of housing at 22% and leisure at 20%, and it also devoted the highest proportion to education, at 11%. However, it allocated only 3% to health, the smallest share for this category, whereas Country E spent 12%, four times as much. Education was a minor expense elsewhere, falling as low as 2% in Country C.
samples.why: Clear overview capturing the general pattern and the outlier · figures selected purposefully with accurate ratios · very well-managed cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary · wide range of structures used accurately.
